text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Parliament should not try to be a board of directors and interfere in the details of the government's work, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said in a weekend radio interview.
- While waiting for Finland's decision on the building of more nuclear power capacity, industry-owned power group Teollisuuden Voima is making plans with foreign companies for a new nuclear plant.
- Accidents at home and on the job are most likely occur in July, statistics show.
KAUPPALEHTI
Kone Oy's director for the Asia-Pacific region Neil Padden says Kone aims for significant market share in Asia and sees Far East sales growing 35 percent this year to 890 million markka.
- Regional power utilities Savon Voima and Kuopion Energia set to merge -- if Espoon Sahko also joins the new group, it would be Finland's second biggest regional power producer.
- Finnish forest industry will need to increase wood imports sharply if timber prices are not brought under control, says industry federation chief Matti Korhonen.

- Finnlines unit Finncarriers' CEO Asser Ahleskog calls for port investment to be focused on southern Finnish harbours, and warns that Finland could miss its chance in the Russian transit business if port development is haphazard.
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Lipponen says the president still has the last say in foreign policy, despite a proposal by parliament's constitutional affairs committee to limit presidential powers.
- Public library in the town of Vantaa has begun passing overdue book notices to a collection agency, which sometimes charges borrowers hundreds of markka for late books.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish police to begin registering DNA samples of people suspected or convicted of serious crimes.

- Finnish Confederation of Industry and Employers (TT) is disappointed with the outcome of the EU's Amsterdam summit -- companies wanted EU to stress competitiveness of European industry, says TT's Brussels bureau chief Kari Jalas. @
- Finnish javelin thrower Harri Hakkarainen won weekend meet in central Finland with a throw of 86.48 metres.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Producing more nuclear power is an option for Finland and one way to meet the international emissions standards, says Conservative party secretary Maija Perho.
- Even the elderly are leaving the scattered settlements of rural Finland to move to towns.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
